item.content:encoded:
This effect lasts until SCP-180 has selected a new host.

Once SCP-180 has stolen the identity of a host subject, when SCP-180 is placed upon any other subject's head, the identity of the first subject (host) is imprinted on the second subject.

What? Does this mean that the first subject gets their "identity" back, thus creating "two" versions of them in the world? Otherwise, if this "loss" is permanent, shouldn't Agent Spunged be held up as a horrifying cautionary tale rather than a fun little example?

Looked through older versions, and I think the "host"-this, "host"-that stuff is still worded weird. Saw a question earlier regarding how it works that wasn't answered.

So Person 1 becomes the Host, and Person 2 looks like Person 1… what happens when Person 3 dons the thing? Do they suddenly look like Person 2/Person 2 becomes the Host, and Person 1 is freed?

Or does Person 3 become the new Host, Persons 1 & 2 are no longer affected at all, and Person 4 ends up looking like Person 3 after putting SCP-180 on their head?

E: +1, btw. Definitely like it, just had that "issue" with it. Just a tad confused on the stages of progression.
